value: LTAA had less total cortical gray matter than NAC. No significant group differences were found for the frontal, limbic, and temporal lobes, whereas LTAA had significantly lower gray matter volumes than NAC for the occipital and parietal lobes and the insula.

Within the occipital lobe, the visual association area and primary visual cortex had less gray matter in LTAA than NAC. Within the parietal lobe, the lateral and mesial parietal areas exhibited reduced gray matter volumes in LTAA. Other areas with significantly decreased gray matter volumes in LTAA were the primary somatosensory cortex, primary motor cortex, and anterior cingulate.
